stories.headline: Jobless rate 5% in Sept vs 5.2% year ago: PLFS
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's unemployment rate (UR) fell to 5% in Sept, compared with 5.2% a year ago, even as the labour force participation rate (LFPR) improved in the country, particularly in rural areas, according to the monthly periodic labour force survey (PLFS) bulletin released Thursday. Sequentially, the UR for people aged 15 and above remained steady at 5% for the second straight month.
The monthly bulletin measures labour market indicators in the current weekly status (CWS), which asks the respondents about their work-related condition in the past seven days. A person is classified as employed if she worked for at least one hour in this reference period.
LFPR, which represents the share of people either working or seeking work, improved to 50.7% in urban areas as compared to 50.4% in Aug, while urban women's participation rose to its highest level (25.9%) since Oct 2025. Urban women's unemployment, however, rose to 9.2% in Sept from 8.9% in Aug, which drove overall joblessness among women to 5.2% from 5.1% during this period. tnn

stories.headline: Exports up 23%, trade deficit at $30 billion in September
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's goods trade deficit narrowed to $30.2 billion in Sept, from $33 billion a year ago, as exports grew 23% to $44.4 billion, while imports rose 8% to $74.6 billion.
On a cumulative basis too, the trade deficit for goods and services narrowed to $13.3 billion in Sept, improving from $14.2 billion a year ago, as growth in exports outpaced the imports growth during the month. Data released by the commerce department Thursday showed that exports stood at $80.8 billion, while monthly imports remained at $94 billion for the month.
Sept marked the second straight month of over 20% export growth, powered by a surge in shipments of electronics (70% jump to $5.3 billion, engineering goods (21% to over $12 billion) and petroleum products (32% to $6.2 billion). Exports are maintaining their growth trend, said commerce secretary Rajesh Agarwal.
On the import front, gold and fertiliser provided much-needed relief, partly due to cooling global prices. Fertiliser imports fell 22.2% to $1.8 billion, while high duties took the sheen off yellow metal shipments, at least through the official channels, with imports falling 81% to $1.8 billion. Silver too fell 49% to 665 million.
There was no respite from high electronic imports, which jumped 51.5% to almost $15 billion, while high oil prices meant crude shipments were 31% higher at $18.3 billion.
Countries like Singapore, the US, and Malaysia recorded strong positive growth as top monthly export destinations.
Trade with China rose about 29%to $91.8 billion in April-Sept, making Beijing the largest trading partner in the first half, with the US ranked second. Exports to China rose 36% to $11 billion, while imports grew 27.8%to 80.3 billion.

stories.headline: Experts’ poll: RBI may hike rates by 0.25% in October policy amid inflationary pressures
stories.deck: The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25% to 6.50%
stories.bodyText:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is likely to increase the repo rate by 0.25% in the October monetary policy review due to mounting inflationary pressure amid the re-escalation of the West Asia crisis and also the rate hikes by global central banks, according to economists and bankers.
If the RBI increases the rate in the upcoming policy, it would mark a reversal in the interest rate policy, which has witnessed rate cuts in 2025 and an extended pause thereafter, according to a PTI poll of 16 economists and bankers.
The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25% to 6.50%; it then kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025. Currently, the RBI's policy repo rate stands at 5.25%.
"Coordination with global central bank hikes, rising inflation risks and strong growth momentum provide policy space to hike," said Kanika Pasricha, Chief Economic Advisor at Union Bank of India.
Further, Dipti Deshpande, principal economist at Crisil, said that since the last policy, inflationary pressures have mounted further mainly due to the re-escalation of the West Asia conflict and the pressure on energy and commodity prices. If these pressures persist, further rate hikes are expected.
A majority of participants in the PTI poll expect a rate hike with a hawkish tone at the upcoming policy review on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). The opinion seems divided on whether there will be a shift in stance.
Sachchidanand Shukla, group chief economist at Larsen & Toubro, however, feels that the RBI will again opt for status quo.
He reasoned that the RBI could wait before raising rates, as there is no evidence yet of demand-led inflation or overheating in the economy.
On the number of rate hikes expected in FY27, experts broadly see at least two increases, with several expecting two to three hikes over the course of the fiscal.
Experts said the RBI may need to gradually normalise its monetary policy stance as headline inflation rises, requiring a rate hike to ensure real interest rates do not turn negative in the coming quarters.
"Gradual normalisation of policy as headline inflation is higher. The rate hike is needed to ensure real rates are not negative in the coming quarters," said Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank.
On the policy stance, experts are divided between 'no change' and 'calibrated tightening', with some also favouring 'withdrawal of accommodation'.
On the policy tone, however, a majority of experts expect a hawkish stance, while a few see the tone as cautious, reflecting concerns over rising inflation and global rate movements.
The experts expect an upward revision to the RBI's FY27 CPI inflation forecast amid elevated crude oil prices, food inflation risks and broadening price pressures.
"The recent surge in crude oil prices to above $100/barrel could likely lead to an increase in the retail selling price (RSP) of petrol and diesel, and further generalisation of price pressures, which would necessitate an upward revision in the CPI inflation forecasts," said Aditi Nayar, chief economist, head-research and outreach at ICRA.
Apoorva Javadekar, chief economist at Shriram Group, said there will be a mild upward revision of 0.10% for Q3 and Q4 of FY27. "In fact, the upward revision to future inflation is almost a pre-condition for a rate hike, as otherwise the inflation is progressing on the projected path."
Rajani Sinha, chief economist at Careedge Ratings, said price pressures are becoming increasingly broad-based, with "around 19% of the 358 items in the CPI basket" recording inflation above 6% in August, up from 13% in March.
India's retail inflation accelerated to an eight-month high of 4.82% in August from 4.45% in July. CPI inflation has stayed above the RBI's 4% target for three straight months, climbing from 3.93% in May to 4.38% in June and 4.45% in July. The August print marked the highest level recorded so far under the new CPI series, which uses 2024 as its base year.
In August monetary policy, the Central bank projected CPI inflation for FY27 at 5.0% with Q2 at 4.7%, Q3 at 5.9%, and Q4 at 5.5%. Inflation for Q1:2027-28 is projected at 5.3%. Core inflation was projected at 4.3% for 2026-27.
On growth, experts largely expect the RBI to revise its FY27 GDP growth forecast upwards, with stronger-than-expected economic activity in the first half of the fiscal supporting the outlook, although some expect no change.
Radhika Rao, Senior Economist and Executive Director at DBS Bank, expects a "slight upward revision to above 7% growth".
The Central bank in its August monetary policy projected real GDP growth for 2026-27 at 6.7%, with Q1 at 7.0%, Q2 at 6.4%, Q3 at 6.5%, and Q4 at 6.8%. Real GDP growth for Q1:2027-28 was projected at 7.3%.
On liquidity management, experts expect the RBI to continue using variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) operations, open market operations (OMOs) and foreign exchange swap operations to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system.

briefs.headline: Government raises deepwater gas price ceiling to $9.89/MMBtu; APM gas cap at $7
briefs.deck: The new ceiling for difficult-field gas, including from the KG-D6 block, is applicable for October 2026 to March 2027, while the APM gas cap for ONGC and OIL’s legacy fields stays at $7 per MMBtu
briefs.bodyText:
The government has raised the ceiling price for natural gas produced from difficult fields, such as the KG-D6 block of Reliance Industries and BP, to $9.89 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) for the six months beginning October 1, 2026, from $8.90 previously, while keeping the ceiling for gas produced from the legacy fields of state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India Limited (OIL) at $7 per MMBtu.
The new ceiling for gas from deepwater, ultra-deepwater and high-pressure, high-temperature discoveries is applicable for the period from October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027, according to a notification by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the oil ministry.
Gas produced from such difficult areas enjoys marketing and pricing freedom under the government's policy, but is subject to a government-notified ceiling.
The higher ceiling could provide some relief to producers developing India's more technically challenging offshore gas resources, where production costs are generally higher than those from mature onshore and legacy fields.
For gas produced by ONGC and OIL from their nomination fields, the government has notified an Administered Price Mechanism (APM) price of $11.22 per MMBtu for October, but the actual price remains capped at $7 per MMBtu, according to PPAC.
The APM gas price applies to gas produced from the legacy fields of the two state-owned companies and is used by priority sectors including city gas distribution, fertiliser and power.
For gas produced from new wells of ONGC and OIL in their nomination blocks, the government allows a 10% premium over the prevailing APM gas price, subject to the applicable ceiling. With the APM price for October capped at $7 per MMBtu, the effective price for new-well gas would accordingly be up to $7.70 per MMBtu.
The higher price for new-well gas is aimed at incentivising ONGC and OIL to invest in developing additional reserves and bringing new production on stream, while maintaining the existing ceiling for gas from their older, legacy fields.
India follows separate pricing mechanisms for gas from legacy fields of national oil companies and newer discoveries in difficult areas.
In April 2023, the government shifted pricing of gas from legacy fields to a formula linked to 10% of the monthly average crude oil import price, subject to a floor and ceiling. The ceiling was initially fixed at $6.50 per MMBtu and was subsequently raised by $0.25 annually after a two-year freeze.
The APM ceiling was raised to $6.75 per MMBtu from April 2025 and moved to $7 in April 2026.
Before the 2023 reform, APM gas prices were revised every six months based on international gas benchmarks and had fluctuated sharply, ranging from $1.79 per MMBtu in 2021 to $8.57 in the six months ended March 2023.
The separate regime for deepwater and other difficult fields was introduced to encourage investment in India's technically challenging hydrocarbon resources by allowing producers greater pricing and marketing flexibility.
Reliance Industries and its partner BP produce gas from the KG-D6 block in the Krishna-Godavari basin, one of India's key deepwater gas-producing areas.
Natural gas is a key feedstock for fertiliser production and is also used in power generation and by city gas distributors to supply compressed natural gas (CNG) and piped natural gas (PNG). Changes in domestic gas prices can therefore affect input costs across these sectors.

briefs.headline: Land shortage cripples Agriculture Ministry’s weather network rollout
briefs.deck: Project is a year behind deadline, with over 96% of planned rain gauges and weather stations yet to be installed; private partners say IMD is retrospectively insisting that sensors be installed on the ground, not on rooftops
briefs.bodyText:
An ambitious public-private partnership project by an Agriculture Ministry body to install automatic rain gauges and automatic weather stations in States is proceeding at a crawl, with completion rates in the single digits and at least a year behind deadline. Over 96% of planned sensors are yet to be installed.
The reason, companies tasked with the implementation say, is a paucity of land to install these weather stations and an alleged “retrospective” insistence by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) that these sensors be set up on the ground rather than on rooftops.
The Weather Information Network and Data System (WINDS) is a programme to set up a nationwide network of weather sensors to supply hyper-local weather data. This is mainly to aid in computing insurance estimates and payouts under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). It is run by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, and executed through the Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC).
Over 50,000 sensors planned
Under the WINDS network, the States, through their implementing private partners, are required to set up the sensor network. The Hindu could confirm that three companies — Skymet Weather Services; Ingen Technologies Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Weather Risk Management Services; and Azista Industries — were collectively asked to instal 1,197 automatic weather stations (AWSs) and 49,313 automatic rain gauges (ARGs), or about 50,500 sensors in all.
An ARG measures rainfall only, though about 10% of ARGs at the gram panchayat level also carry a temperature sensor. An AWS measures rainfall along with air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and wind direction. Data from these sensors flow into data centres run by government agencies, to prepare hourly, daily, and fortnightly forecasts.
Majority of proposed sites rejected
According to documents viewed by The Hindu, Uttar Pradesh was to have installed 27,487 ARGs — over half the ARG target — followed by Uttarakhand (7,983), Odisha (7,286), Assam (2,140), and Himachal Pradesh (about 3,550).
For AWSs, Odisha’s target was the largest at 434, ahead of Assam (196), U.P. (157), and Kerala (148). According to a status update on September 9 — the latest that The Hindu was able to confirm — the network has delivered 113 AWSs (9.4% of target) and 1,730 ARGs (4%), leaving a shortfall of about 48,700 (96%).
The bottleneck is mostly site selection rather than hardware, the documents reveal. Of the 27,644 sites in U.P., 16,478 were rejected. In Odisha, 5,666 of 7,720 sites were rejected, while 524 of 946 sites were rejected in Kerala. The documents also flag hundreds of “duplicate sites” that were approved at the panchayat and block level but need re-checking, sites pending clearances, and those which the States have yet to share with the implementing partners.
Retrospective changes
A representative of one of the private partner companies, who asked not to be named, told The Hindu that the delays stem from a shortage of suitable land and from the requirement that rain gauges be placed on the ground rather than on rooftops. He blamed changes made to the WINDS guidelines “retrospectively.”
The manual published on September 1, 2023 allowed an ARG to be placed on the roof of a single-storey building where siting requirements could not be met or in flood-prone areas, he claimed, adding that the IMD had approved this as a member of the WINDS Committee. About two and a half years later, and after six States had already issued tenders or work orders, the Agriculture Department amended the manual on the IMD’s advice on December 3, 2025, to retroactively limit rooftop ARGs to just 10% to 15% of the total, he said.
‘Height affects weather data’
IMD officials contend that the requirement that ARGs and AWSs be located on the ground is “essential” to ensure that the data collected is accurate.
“The underlying principle – and this is a requirement of the World Meteorological Organisation whose guidelines we adhere to – is that sensors must be on the ground and only in exceptional situations be situated on rooftops. Height significantly affects weather data,” S. Hosalikar, a former senior meteorologist with the IMD and a member of the 2023 committee, told The Hindu.
The 2023 document says: “ARGs shall be located on a level piece of ground, covered with short grass or natural earth,” ideally 4x3 metres in size. “If suitable siting requirements are not met or in case of flood prone areas,” the ARG can go on “the rooftop of the one-story building… rooftop units need a stable foundation and a tamper-proof setup,” adds the document, which was perused by The Hindu.
Cap on rooftop sensors
The manual sets no numerical cap on rooftop units. This only appears in the 2025 amendment which specifies a 10% cap. It also requires that rooftop installations be allowed only if States issue a justification note saying there is no suitable ground space. In flood- or landslide-prone regions, the ceiling is 15%, with prior State recommendation and approval sent to the WINDS Committee.
“Measuring rainfall from the top of the building and from the ground makes a significant difference as some part of falling rain evaporates. Secondly, a consistent network of ground-based sensors is necessary to ensure standardised data, which is difficult to achieve if sensors are on rooftops (with variable heights). India lives in its villages and it should not be that challenging to get small plots of land,” IMD director general M. Mohapatra told The Hindu. He underlined that the IMD was only a technical partner for the project and was not administering it.
The Hindu reached out to Soumya Bandopadhyay, director of the MNCFC, the nodal agency in charge of the project, seeking a comment but did not get any response till the time of going to press.

briefs.headline: Korea to explore business opportunities in Karnataka sectors
briefs.deck: Enthused by K-pop, K-dramas, Korean cosmetics, Korean products, Karnataka offers market access, talent and innovation partnerships to Korean delegation
briefs.bodyText:
A high-level business delegation from the Republic of Korea met Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Information Technology, Biotechnology, and e-Governance, here on Saturday to explore opportunities for investment, business expansion, and technology partnerships between Korea and Karnataka.
The discussions focused on strengthening Korea-Karnataka business linkages and creating practical pathways for Korean companies and investors to enter and scale in the Indian market through Karnataka, said a release.

briefs.headline: India’s current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August, RBI data shows
briefs.deck: India's overall balance of payments showed a surplus of $45.4 billion in August 2026. This significant surplus is attributed to an increase in foreign currency inflows, especially from non-resident Indian deposits. The current account deficit also narrowed slightly to $5.2 billion during the same month. Foreign direct investment improved, with net inflows of $3.3 billion recorded.
briefs.bodyText:
India’s overall balance of payments (BoP) recorded a surplus of $45.4 billion in August 2026, compared with a deficit of $5.6 billion in the same month last year, as foreign currency inflows, particularly non-resident Indian (NRI) deposits, rose sharply, according to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data.
The overall BoP surplus also increased from $20.8 billion in July 2026, reflecting a sharp improvement in the country’s external financial position despite a continuing current account deficit.
Banking capital inflows were a major contributor to the turnaround, reaching $64.7 billion in August, compared with an outflow of $4.7 billion in August 2025. Within this category, net NRI deposits surged to $83 billion during the month, against $1 billion in the corresponding period last year, the data showed.
The increase in foreign currency inflows followed measures introduced by the RBI earlier this year to attract overseas funds and strengthen India’s external position.
Current account deficit narrows in August
India’s current account deficit narrowed to $5.2 billion in August from $6.1 billion a year earlier, even as the merchandise trade deficit remained substantial.
The merchandise trade deficit stood at $26.6 billion during the month, compared with $27.6 billion in August 2025.
Services trade continued to provide support, with the services surplus rising to $16.5 billion from $15.6 billion in the same month last year.
Foreign direct investment (FDI) also improved, recording net inflows of $3.3 billion in August, compared with a net outflow of $0.1 billion a year earlier.
Foreign portfolio investment (FPI) registered net inflows of $1.7 billion during the month, reversing net outflows of $2.6 billion recorded in August 2025.
However, the cumulative figures for April-August showed continued pressure on the current account. The deficit widened to $18.3 billion during the five-month period, from $12.8 billion in the corresponding period last year.
Despite this, India recorded an overall BoP surplus of $58 billion during April-August 2026, compared with a deficit of $0.8 billion a year earlier, according to the RBI data.
RBI clarifies foreign exchange reserve requirements
Separately, the RBI has clarified that its new Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) requirements apply only to specified foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the purchase of foreign currency against the rupee.
In a detailed set of frequently asked questions released on Thursday, the central bank said the reserve requirement would not apply to derivative contracts in which users sell foreign currency against the domestic currency.
The RBI announced the regulatory measures, including the introduction of FERR, on October 10 against the backdrop of significant depreciation in the rupee. The domestic currency has strengthened against the US dollar since the announcement.
FERR is a reserve that authorised dealers must maintain with the RBI for qualifying rupee-based foreign exchange derivative contracts. The requirement covers specified contracts undertaken by authorised dealers with users, as well as contracts used to hedge currency risks arising from their own assets and liabilities.
The central bank said the requirement applies to specified derivative contracts between authorised dealers and users with a notional value exceeding the equivalent of $2 million.
"Accordingly, a derivative contract having a notional value of $2 million equivalent or less undertaken by an authorised dealer with a user is not subject to the requirement," the RBI said in its FAQs.
The RBI defines a user as any person resident in India or outside the country, other than an authorised dealer.
The central bank also cautioned authorised dealers against attempts to structure derivative transactions to avoid the provisions.
The FERR clarification comes as the RBI seeks to regulate specified foreign exchange derivative exposures while its latest balance of payments figures show a sharp rise in overseas inflows during August.

briefs.headline: Unemployment rate in country stands at 5% in September, stable compared to August: NSO
briefs.deck: The rural unemployment rate remains “broadly stable” at 4.2% against 4.1% in August, while urban rate marginally rises from 6.8% in August to 6.9% in this month
briefs.bodyText:
The Unemployment Rate (UR) in the country stood at 5% in September, stable compared to August, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National Statistics Office (NSO). The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said here in a release on Thursday that the rural UR remained “broadly stable” at 4.2%, against 4.1% in August, while urban UR marginally rose from 6.8% in August to 6.9% in this month. “Compared with September 2025, the overall UR declined by 0.2 percentage points and reached at 5% in September 2026. Rural UR declined by 0.4 percentage points, from 4.6% in September, 2025 to 4.2% in September 2026. UR in urban areas remained broadly stable from 6.8% in September 2025 to 6.9% in September 2026,” the Ministry said.
Among females, the overall UR remained at 5.2%, up from 5.1% in August. Rural female UR stood at 3.9%, which, according to the government, is its lowest level in 2026, while urban female UR rose marginally from 8.9% to 9.2%. The government said unemployment rates declined year-on-year for both genders. The PLFS is the primary source of data on labour force participation and employment and unemployment conditions. At the all-India level, the monthly estimates are based on information collected from 3,70,513 persons surveyed.
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), for persons aged 15 years and above, remained at 55.5% in September, compared to 55.6% in August. “In rural areas, LFPR was recorded at 58% against 58.2% in August 2026, while the urban LFPR registered a moderate increase of 0.3 percentage points, rising from 50.4% in August, 2026 to 50.7% in September 2026,” the Ministry said. Compared to September 2025, the overall LFPR increased by 0.2 percentage points, from 55.3% to 55.5%. The rural LFPR increased by 0.6 percentage points in one year, from 57.4% to 58%, while urban LFPR registered a marginal decline of 0.2 percentage points, from 50.9% to 50.7%. Overall female LFPR stood at 34.6% in September 2026, compared with 34.8% in August 2026. “Urban female LFPR recorded a notable month-on-month increase of 0.5 percentage points, rising from 25.4% to 25.9% and reaching its highest level since October 2025. Rural female LFPR estimated at 38.9% in September 2026 against 39.4% in the previous month,” the release added. Overall female LFPR increased by 0.5 percentage points, from 34.1% in September 2025 to 34.6% in September 2026.
The overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) remained at 52.7% in September 2026, compared with 52.8% in August 2026. Overall WPR increased by 0.3 percentage points, from 52.4% in September 2025 to 52.7% in September 2026.

briefs.headline: RBI chief lays down 5 key priorities to maintain financial stability amidst emerging risks
briefs.deck: “Financial instability anywhere can become a threat to financial stability everywhere”.
briefs.bodyText:
As multiple shocks threaten financial stability Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday emphasised the importance of maintaining it at all costs.
Financial instability anywhere can become a threat to financial stability everywhere, he pointed out.
The challenge before financial sector regulators is to build a financial system that can withstand the shocks they anticipate and those, they cannot yet foresee, said Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) while laying down five key priorities that policymakers must factor in when safeguarding financial stability.
“This requires resilient institutions, better data, deeper markets, credible safety nets, effective resolution mechanisms and regulation and supervision that are proactive and forward-looking, while being proportionate,” he said in his special address at the Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave, on the topic “Preserving Financial Stability in an Evolving World”.
Firstly, stating that some shocks will be inevitable, he said financial stability was not about preventing them, it’s about strengthening systemic resilience to face those shocks and contain their amplification.
“Shocks may be endogenous or exogenous. Our aim must be to foster a financial system that can provide financial services in all states of the world, even under severe shocks,” he said.
Secondly, as a new generation of systemic risks were taking shape, he said assessing them and their complex interactions was vital.
“Risks are increasingly exogenous, cross-border and interconnected. The next financial crisis may not originate in a bank, or even in finance. It may begin with a geopolitical event, a cyberattack, or a technological failure and affect the financial system through multiple channels,” he cautioned.
To strengthen systemic resilience, those responsible must aim to better understand the network of dependencies and contagion channels and make scenario analysis a cornerstone of risk management.
Thirdly, monitoring and assessment frameworks must improve. “For that, we need better and more granular data. The financial system is becoming increasingly complex, but data on NBFIs, interconnected exposures, technology dependencies and cross-border positions remain fragmented,” the Governor said.
In an increasingly interconnected financial system, the quality of our data would increasingly determine the quality of our risk assessment, he stated.
Fourthly he said, resilience must be system-wide. “A strong banking system is necessary, but not sufficient. We need resilience across sectors and institutions: NBFIs, financial markets, payment systems, technology infrastructure, critical third parties and cross-border financial networks,” he emphasised.
“Financial instability anywhere can become a threat to financial stability everywhere,” he pointed out. Fifth, he said, innovation must strengthen, not fragment, the foundations of trust.
“Artificial intelligence, tokenisation, and new forms of financial intermediation can dramatically improve efficiency. But innovation will be sustainable only if the financial system preserves the fundamental properties on which trust rests: sound institutions, settlement finality, singleness of money, and financial integrity,” Mr Malhotra stated.
“If we succeed, financial stability will remain largely invisible. And, in central banking, invisibility is perhaps the most meaningful measure of success,” he highlighted.

briefs.headline: Titan Company deepens focus on mechanical horology as category grows almost 5-fold
briefs.deck: Newly launched platform Vetra will allow Titan to progressively develop capabilities across different mechanical functions and propositions, including open-heart constructions, GMT and date complications to cater to growing consumer appreciation for craftsmanship and engineering: Titan Watches CEO (pic shared)
briefs.bodyText:
Mechanical watchmaking is entering an important phase in India, driven by a growing consumer appreciation for craftsmanship, engineering and the experience of owning a watch with a mechanical heart, said Kuruvilla Markose, CEO, Watches at Titan Company Ltd.
The context: India, also global markets, is undergoing a massive structural shift away from mass-market quartz watches to premium mechanical and automatic watches. Although, quartz still dominates the overall sales volumes because of its affordability, consumer interest for deeply designed wares, fast-pace of growth and value are heavily tilting toward mechanical horology, as watches have emerged to fashion or lifestyle statements from just being from a mere time-showing devices. A quartz watch is an electronic device powered by a battery, whereas a mechanical watch is a micro-engine powered by a tightly wound spring.
“We have seen the category gain significant momentum, with Titan’s mechanical watch business growing nearly fivefold over the last three years,’’ Mr. Markose told The Hindu.
Titan is expecting the segment to grow from around ₹270 crore last year to approximately ₹350 crore end of the current fiscal. “The broader opportunity is also being shaped by premiumisation, with watches above ₹25,000 growing at a significantly faster pace than the overall market,’’ he added.
To add momentum to growth of this rapidly expanding segment, Titan Company is making a strategic push into premium mechanical watchmaking by designing and branding its own in-house movement, Vetra. It embodies Titan’s philosophy of elegant ingenuity anchored in solving the most demanding challenges with clarity, precision and purpose, bringing artistry and mechanics into a single, cohesive whole. This bold venture allows the company to develop advanced precision engineering capabilities while significantly strengthening its presence in the competitive global horology market.
According to Mr. Markose, Vetra is Titan’s branded in-house automatic movement platform, built around the 7A architecture, which provides a common mechanical foundation from which the company can develop different watch propositions and complications. ``Having greater ownership of the movement gives our engineering and design teams more flexibility to develop the movement and the watch together, rather than designing around the limitations of an externally sourced catalogue movement,’’ he explained adding, this allowed Titan to progressively develop capabilities across different mechanical functions and propositions, including open-heart constructions, GMT and date complications.
He further said, Titan Automatics was the consumer expression of this capability, bringing together different applications of the Vetra platform. The collection includes the Infinium, which uses the Vetra 7A20+ movement with a 72-hour power reserve, alongside other propositions such as Dualis, Midnite and Atrium. “The move from our earlier 7000-series mechanical platforms, which generally offered around 36 to 40 hours of running time, to a 72-hour power reserve represents a meaningful step in our mechanical movement capability,’’ he claimed. The longer reserve has involved optimisation of how energy was stored and delivered within the movement, including the barrel and mainspring arrangement, he explained.
Every Vetra movement was assembled by hand and individually tested, and Titan was continuing to deepen its capabilities across this value chain. Movement R&D, precision component manufacturing, tooling, assembly and validation all need to come together to produce sophisticated mechanical movements consistently and at scale. ``Our larger ambition is to create watches that are imagined in India, engineered in India and built with the capabilities to engage consumers around the world. Vetra and Titan Automatics were an important part of that journey, as the company continued to build the engineering and manufacturing depth that could help India establish a stronger presence in modern horology, Mr. Markose further said.
The new collection of watches, designed on Vetra platform, were expected to offer watch connoisseurs and enthusiasts an experience of a new expression of Titan’s mechanical watchmaking, where the craft of the movement would be as much a part of the experience as the watch itself, said the Bengaluru-based watch manufacturer.
Earlier, officially announcing Vetra, Rahul Shukla, Vice-President and Chief Sales & Marketing Officer- Watches Division at Titan Company said, “Vetra firmly places Titan within a relatively small global community of watchmakers building in-house mechanical capabilities, while contributing to the emergence of a stronger indigenous horological ecosystem in India.’’
More importantly, it marked a significant stride in strengthening the country’s position in modern horology, Mr. Shukla added.
Other Titan Company officials at a factory-visit (Hosur) organised for the media fraternity recently said: For more than four decades, Titan, has pursued watchmaking with an ambition that extends well beyond the dial. Each milestone has brought greater depth in craft, engineering and innovation, evolving beyond the creation of timepieces to forge a distinct horological identity as much for the brand as for India’s emerging watchmaking stature.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen washes away frustrations with win at Bahrain Grand Prix
stories.deck: The ​four-time Formula 1 drivers’ champion earned his first win of 2026 ‌and the 72nd of his decorated career
stories.bodyText:
Max Verstappen flushed away at least some of his seasonlong frustrations Sunday (October 4, 2026) by winning the rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
The four-time Formula 1 drivers’ champion earned his first win of 2026 and the 72nd of his decorated career when he waited out a 1-hour, 33-minute delay at the outset and then held off current drivers’ standings leader Kimi Antonelli at the finish.
George Russell, who was still alive with an outside chance at catching Mercedes AMG Motorsport teammate Antonelli for the drivers’ title, saw those hopes take a blow due to an engine failure with five laps remaining.
After a season in which Verstappen struggled to adapt to changes to F1 cars, the rest of the field was able to feel his pain for a day. Those new cars struggled to operate in the wet conditions, leading to an initial 40-minute delay at the start and then another 53-minute delay when software issues plagued some cars, including Verstappen’s.
“It was very hectic with a lot of different things in the start,” Verstappen said. “No power, so you have to wait for the power to kick in. But then we made the right call with the intermediates, and after that, step by step, we moved our way forward.”
When the race finally started, Verstappen dropped from his position on the pole into third place before passing Antonelli on Lap 13, and went on to win from there, finishing 2.3 seconds ahead of the standings leader. Lewis Hamilton was third after rallying from 18th place.
“It’s a really nice one, after the year that we’ve had and the progression that we’ve made,” Verstappen said. “I’m incredibly proud of everyone, and it’s just super nice to win here.”
Charles Leclerc finished fourth, while Isack Hadjar was fifth.
Hadjar was one of the first drivers to be impacted by the early conditions when he lost control on Turn 2 of the formation lap and was forced into the gravel. Verstappen and Hamilton then reported engine issues.
A red flag was issued as drivers took a more cautious approach than usual in the early going.
Russell’s issues arrived after Alexander Albon saw his car stall. With the safety car on the track on Lap 43, Russell came to a stop just before heading into Turn 1.
Verstappen maintained his lead on the restart and went on to the victory.

stories.headline: Punam Raut, part of India's 2017 World Cup run, retires from international cricket
stories.deck: The 37-year-old represented India in four Tests, 73 ODIs and 35 T20Is between 2009 and 2021.
stories.bodyText:
Out-of-favour India women's cricket team top-order batter Punam Raut on Thursday announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket with immediate effect.
The 37-year-old represented India in four Tests, 73 ODIs and 35 T20Is between 2009 and 2021.
“After much thought and reflection, I have decided to retire from international cricket in all formats of the game,” Raut said in a post on her Instagram page.
"Representing India has been the greatest honour of my life. Cricket has been more than just a sport — it has shaped my character, taught me resilience, and given me memories that I will cherish forever. Every time I wore the India jersey, I did so with immense pride and gratitude.
“Wearing the India jersey was a dream that became a reality, and I will always be grateful for the trust and support I received.”
Raut also thanked the Mumbai Cricket Association for its role in her development as a cricketer.
“My sincere thanks to the Mumbai Cricket Association for believing in me during my formative years. The opportunities and guidance I received there laid the foundation of my cricketing journey,” Raut said.
She scored 2,299 runs in 73 ODIs, 719 runs in 35 T20Is and 264 runs in four Tests. Her international career included four centuries — three in ODIs and one in a Test against South Africa in 2014 — along with 15 ODI half-centuries and four in T20Is. Her last international appearance was in an ODI against England in June 2021.
One of Raut's most memorable performances came during India's run to the 2017 Women's World Cup final. She scored 381 runs in the tournament, including 86 against England in the final at Lord's, which India lost by nine runs.
During the same World Cup, Raut scored 109 against Ireland and shared a record 320-run opening partnership with Deepti Sharma.
In 2021, Raut was part of India's historic pink-ball Test against Australia. She scored 36 in the first innings and earned praise for walking off after edging a delivery despite being given not out.

briefs.headline: England crush Croatia 7-0 as Spain stay perfect with Czech victory
briefs.deck: England ⁠are second in League A, Group Three with six points from three matches, behind Spain on nine
briefs.bodyText:
Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice apiece as England demolished Luka Modric's Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday, but Spain stayed three points clear at the top of their Nations League group with a 3-1 victory over the Czech Republic.
Jude Bellingham scored once and provided three assists for England, with Anthony Gordon and substitute Morgan Rogers also on target in a performance captain Kane described as "unbelievable".
England are second in League A, Group Three with six points from three matches, behind Spain on nine. Croatia have three points and the Czechs remain pointless.
"Unbelievable from start to finish," Kane told ITV. "We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game from start to finish, being completely dominant with the ball and without the ball. That was it right there."
Kane took his international tally to 89 goals in 124 appearances, moving within one cap of Peter Shilton's England record.
Asked about potentially drawing level with Shilton against the Czech Republic on Tuesday, Kane said: "Would be nice. That is why he (manager Thomas Tuchel) takes me off, to save me for the next one!"
England went ahead after little more than seven minutes when Josko Gvardiol lost possession and Bellingham released Kane, who slipped between two defenders and fired home.
Bellingham doubled the lead in the 21st minute after Gordon turned Saka's cross back across goal. Gordon added the third in the 39th, meeting Jarell Quansah's cross with a first-time finish.
Mateo Kovacic squandered a close-range chance before Bellingham crossed for an unmarked Saka to score a minute before halftime.
Elliot Anderson supplied Kane's second goal with a low cross in the 53rd minute, before Josip Stanisic's misplaced pass across his own box gifted Saka another goal in the 68th.
Bellingham released Rogers to complete the rout three minutes from time.
"They couldn't live with our pace, with our runs," Kane said.
SPAIN KEEP WINNING
World and European champions Spain maintained their perfect start in Oviedo despite coach Luis de la Fuente making nine changes to the side that beat Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday.
Lamine Yamal opened the scoring in the sixth minute, curling a stunning left-footed shot into the top corner from the edge of the box.
After Spain squandered several opportunities, captain Rodri doubled their advantage by converting a rebound inside the area, his first international goal in more than two years.
Jiri Slama gave the visitors hope in the 69th minute, finishing a swift counter-attack with an angled shot just inside David Raya's right post.
Their chances of an equaliser faded when Ladislav Krejci received a second booking in the 85th minute for holding back an opponent to stop a counter-attack.
Mikel Merino then sealed Spain's victory, finishing first time from inside the box following another quick break.
In League B, Scotland won 2-0 at North Macedonia through goals from Kieron Bowie and John McGinn before Scott McKenna was sent off in the 83rd minute.
Switzerland came from behind to beat Slovenia 2-1 in Luzern, with an Erik Janza own goal and Dan Ndoye's strike overturning Zan Vipotnik's opener. The Swiss lead Group One on nine points, with Scotland and Slovenia level on four.

briefs.headline: IND vs WI ODIs review: Men in Blue’s bowling remains a red mark even as batters extend purple patch
briefs.deck: Apart from Kuldeep in the first match, none of the bowlers looked like they could keep the batters honest or provide timely breakthroughs
briefs.bodyText:
With just about a year to go for the 2027 ODI World Cup, India’s preparation for the quadrennial event got off on the right note as it posted a 2-1 series win over the West Indies.
There were, however, some warning signs that the team will want to address soon.
The big positive was the batting. The top-order set up the series victory, led by skipper Shubman Gill, who scored two centuries, including a double hundred.
More importantly, Rohit Sharma (225 runs) and Virat Kohli (168) were on song. Since this is the only format they play, it is imperative the senior duo maximises every opportunity.
K.L. Rahul got only one chance and proved why he is so vital to the team, scoring an unbeaten 129, even if it went in vain.
However, bowling remains a concern. Granted, the pitches at all three venues had very little for the bowlers. Still, the attack is hardly settled.
Apart from Kuldeep Yadav in the first match, none of the others looked like they could keep the batters honest or provide timely breakthroughs.
The other fast bowlers not being able to take up responsibility showed how the Men in Blue are over-reliant on Jasprit Bumrah, who was away on Asian Games duty.
The management handed out debuts to Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj, both of whom proved expensive while Mohammed Siraj’s recent struggle continued in the only match he played. Captain Gill admitted as much, saying he would have wanted to see more out of his speedsters.
“Bowling in the PowerPlay and in the death has been hurting us. If you don’t get off to a good start in the PowerPlay, it’s not easy to take wickets in the middle overs as we have seen,” said Gill.
“It’s not easy to create chances with only four fielders outside. The intensity of the game, and how it goes, becomes completely different if you don’t keep taking wickets in either the PowerPlay or the middle overs,” he added.
Going forward, the think-tank needs to quickly identify the right combination for the World Cup and give them enough games to get into a groove, something Gill stressed he wants to do from the next series.

briefs.headline: U-23 cricket | Andre Siddarth backs Tamil Nadu team to extend its dominance
briefs.bodyText:
The Tamil Nadu u-23 team just cannot stop clinching titles. Having achieved a double in the previous season, it added a trophy to its cabinet after defeating Rest of India u-23 in a match that mirrored the Irani Cup.
C. Andre Siddarth, who led the State to its latest triumph on Sunday, believes the current crop is capable of extending its dominance. “They have experience... the way they won the tournaments last year speaks for itself. They are good enough to win the tournaments again,” said Andre, proudly sporting a victor’s medal around his neck.
The u-23 unit will begin its Col. C.K. Nayudu Trophy defence in a home game against Saurashtra in Dindigul later this month. With Andre becoming a mainstay in the senior red-ball set-up, the age-group side will be led by all-rounder S. Mohamed Ali. “These guys are too good to be honest. I have been playing with them since my u-12 days. They know what they need to do... these aren’t guys who need to be told what is expected of them,” Andre added.
For RoI opener Angkrish Raghuvanshi, it was about getting back in the groove.
The Mumbai lad had been out of action for three months with a finger injury, but he is now finding his feet again. The double century against TN u-23 was a massive confidence booster. “I am playing [competitive cricket] after a long time and my knock gave me clarity. The middle of the pitch is my happy place,” said Raghuvanshi.
“I tried to bat as long as I could. It was a satisfying experience because every batter dreams of hitting big hundreds. It was a good day for me, but it would have been better had we won the match,” he added.

briefs.headline: Sammy effusive in his praise for Hope’s leadership qualities
briefs.bodyText:
West Indies coach Daren Sammy paid rich compliments to his skipper Shai Hope for carrying the team on his back to beat India in the final ODI here on Saturday.
With regular opener Jewel Andrews unable to bat after injuring his finger while fielding, Hope, who donned the gloves for 50 overs, had to open the innings and carried his bat through, slamming an unbeaten 162.
“He was in the field for what, 98.2 overs. He literally took the team on his back today with the bat, like he’s done so many times before. The skipper stepping up is not anything new to him, but to keep 50 overs and then put on your pads and go and play an innings like that was special,” said Sammy,
“We came here knowing the quality that India has and to measure ourselves against a team like that. We showed that when we do things consistently well for long enough, we could match the number one team in the world. We will take a lot of learning from this.”
Sammy, a two-time T20 World Cup-winning skipper, was also impressed by Hope’s leadership and felt the latter has always led by example.
“He doesn’t really say much. But when he speaks, he’s quite clear as to what he’s expecting from himself and from the group.”
“As I said, he leads by his performance. He believes in that. Like today, somebody had to go up and open, and when I said to him [to open], he didn’t say a word.
“He just put on his pads, went out, and won us the game. I don’t think he gets enough credit for what he’s done for West Indies, how he’s played, and the commitment he’s given us. Class player, great individual,” remarked Sammy.

briefs.headline: It worked out according to my game plan: Pranavi
briefs.deck: Pranavai, who hails from Mysore, returned with a par 70 score in the fourth round and clinched the gold with a four-day aggregate score of 15-under 265
briefs.bodyText:
Pranavi Urs made history by becoming the first Indian woman golfer to win the individual gold at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday.
Pranavai, who hails from Mysuru, returned with a par 70 score in the fourth round and clinched the gold with a four-day aggregate score of 15-under 265.
Pranavi, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar also secured the silver medal in the team event with a combined score of 14-under 546. China bagged the gold while Taiwan the bronze.
Speaking to The Hindu from Nagoya, Pranavi said: “ It’s amazing to win the gold medal and I am happy to be the first one to do it. I didn’t get the start I wanted, but I focused on what to do and took it shot by shot and it worked out according to my game plan.”
The 23-year-old has been competing on the Ladies European Tour for the last three years. She has logged eight top-10 finishes on the Tour.
Pranavi had the distinction of being the first Indian woman to win a professional mixed-gender tournament at the IGPL in Mumbai last November.

briefs.headline: U-19 cricket | India keen to get the job done in second game against Australia
briefs.bodyText:
The India under-19 team has enjoyed a near-perfect couple of weeks, defeating Australia u-19 in three one-day games and a four-day ‘Test’ in Rajkot.
The developmental tour will conclude with the second and final multi-day match, starting at the Narendra Modi Stadium Ground ‘A’ here on Monday.
The hosts have had multiple performers across the multi-format series, with Lakshya Raichandani and Yashbardhan Chauhan leading from the front.
Lakshya, in particular, has had a memorable time. In the previous game, the 17-year-old opener put himself in the record books with 240, the second-highest score by an Indian in youth Tests. His double century helped India post a mammoth 494 and beat Australia by an innings and 48 runs.
Yashbardhan, having scored a half-century, doubled his impact with off-spin. He partnered left-arm slow bowler Ishan Om and kept Australia under pressure. Mohit Ulva, meanwhile, has emerged as a pacer to watch out for.
For Australia, Blake Cattle has been the standout with the bat, scoring centuries in both innings of the previous ‘Test’. Zed Hollick also carried his form into the longer format but could not convert his half-century into a substantial score.
That has largely summed up Australia’s tour so far: promising individual performances that have not sustained for long enough. The final game, therefore, offers another opportunity for the visiting youngsters to build on those flashes of brilliance.
For India, the task would be simple: finish the job well.

briefs.headline: Asian Games | Sayonara Aichi-Nagoya, hello Doha!
briefs.deck: The Olympic Council of Asia torch and flag were handed over to Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, who passed it to Olympic, World and Asian high jump champion Mutaz Essa Barshim as a mark of formal handover
briefs.bodyText:
The flag and the torch were passed, the athletes celebrated and Aichi-Nagoya bid adieu to the Asian Games here on Sunday the way it had started — highlighting Japan’s culture and history and with hopes of sports unifying the continent going forward.
After more than two weeks of intense competition that saw more than 15,000 athletes from 45 countries creating almost 50 world records, the celebratory atmosphere at the Paloma Mizuho Athletic Stadium on Sunday relegated all the logistical nightmares, venue mismanagement and organisational shortcomings to the background.
Olympic Council of Asia President Sheikh Joaan Bin Hamad Al Thani declared the Games officially closed after the 90-minute programme witnessed by Japan’s crown prince and princess. The OCA torch and flag were handed over to Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, who passed it to Olympic, World and Asian high jump champion Mutaz Essa Barshim as a mark of formal handover. Qatari rider Jassim Al Kuwari entered on a horse, took the flag from Barshim and rode out. The next edition is set to be held in Doha in 2030.
“Tonight, as we lower the flag on Aichi-Nagoya 2026, we close these Games but we raise the bar for Asian sport. The flame may be extinguished but the hopes it has ignited will continue to burn brightly across our continent,” Hamad Al Thani said. The empty space at the centre of the rainbow heart logo from the opening ceremony was replaced with ‘One Asia’ for the closing, to highlight the sense of unity.
Neeru leads contingent
A laser show, with performances from artists of the Nagoya school of music and dance, was followed by the athletes parade. The Indian contingent was led by shooter Neeru Dhanda as the flag-bearer, who had to leave Japan and return due to the country’s strict gun laws, who arrived with the other flag-bearers before the rest of the contingents joined accompanied by light and music for the athletes’ parade.
A hexagonal stage placed at the centre of the stadium, adorned with lanterns, saw a bon-odori performance, a traditional Japanese dance transcending age and genders with local singers joining in for a rendition of Matsuken Samba II that finally brought the curtains down on the event.

briefs.headline: Our fielding has not been up to the mark: Gill
briefs.deck: The Indian captain adds that ground fielding needs to get better
briefs.bodyText:
Even as India celebrated yet another home ODI series triumph, skipper Shubman Gill did not hold back on the things the team needs to improve. Foremost among them was the fielding standard, which the captain felt was poor in the three outings against the West Indies.
“I think we dropped around three or four catches today (Saturday). Dropping catches breaks the momentum,” said Gill following his side’s five-wicket loss to West Indies in the third and final ODI here.
“Our fielding in the series, I would say, has not been up to the mark. I think we dropped around seven catches in the whole series, if I’m not wrong.”
Gill also highlighted that ground fielding needs to get better and spoke about how it affects the bowlers.
“Even in the field today, we gave away many runs. We were quite sloppy. I think leading up to the World Cup, these are the areas where we definitely need to get better. We need to be at our best, especially on the field. If the wicket isn’t helping the bowlers and our fielding is substandard, it becomes difficult for them,” he pointed out.
On experimenting with players for the all-rounder’s slots, Gill said, “Anshul (Kamboj) and Auqib (Nabi) are the kind of players who are going to be in the mix a lot. We want someone who can bowl and can bat a bit at No. 8. That number is very crucial for us.”
“But I honestly don’t think there is that much time to experiment. Hopefully we get all the players that are available from the next series, and we want to start playing with the combination that we want for the World Cup”.
